messages:
maya: heads-up — I ran a mixed workload sweep this morning comparing streaming chat vs non-streaming completions with different microbatch sizes. found a p99 tail regression for chat at mb=8 that doesn't appear for completions. attaching quick notes.
aj: can you paste the perf trace / kernel timeline? :eyes:
maya: sure — main highlights:
```
mb=4 streaming chat  -> p95 82ms p99 180ms
mb=8 streaming chat  -> p95 95ms p99 420ms  <-- spike
mb=16 streaming chat -> p95 120ms p99 200ms
mb=8 completions     -> p95 90ms p99 110ms
```

simon: interesting that mb=8 is the worst. looks like a scheduling/kernal choice cliff rather than pure queueing.
li: did the runtime pick a different kernel for the attention op at mb=8? that's a common knee.
maya: yes — trace shows kernel selector switches from kernel_A (fast for small seqs) to kernel_B (optimized for larger batches) right when the avg effective batch hits ~7.5. but kernel_B has a bunch of tail steps for streaming because of KV handling.
perf-bot: profile summary uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/3349990000/summary.html
nidhi: can you paste the nvprof timeline snippet? curious about SM occupancy and memcpy overlap.
maya: here's a trimmed trace (timestamps relative):
```
[0.00s] enqueue reqs (3->8)
[0.08s] kernel_A launch (attention)  (fast path)
[0.18s] kernel_B launch (attention)  (fallback)
[0.18s] kv-serialize memcpy (blocking)  -> +40ms
[0.60s] kernel tail-work loop (looping small launches)
```

aj: kv-serialize memcpy blocking — is that memcpy from device->host or host->device? that could block the stream.
maya: host->device prefetch for missing KV pages. completions path pre-warms KV differently so it avoids the memcpy during generation; streaming chat does handshake per-message so prefetch timing is worse.
simon: so two overlapping issues: kernel_B has extra small-launch tail work + runtime prefetch hits during streaming handshake.
li: does kernel_B require extra temp buffers that increase memcpy work? maybe quant layout differs.
maya: yes, kernel_B expects interleaved quant blocks and we do a small conversion stage that memcpy's a scratch buffer per-request. cost amortizes at mb>=16 but hurts at mid-range where switching happens.
nidhi: do we see higher kernel launch overhead counts for mb=8? small kernels repeated -> p99 tail.
maya: exactly. profiling shows ~12k small kernels for a request at mb=8 stream vs ~3k for mb=4.

aj: two mitigations to try:
- avoid kernel_B when streaming: add runtime hint to prefer kernel_A for streaming sessions until kv warm
- prefetch more aggressively on handshake for streaming requests to move memcpy earlier

simon: also consider hybrid policy: if mb in [6..10] prefer kernel_A; if mb>=12 allow kernel_B. essentially hysteresis around selector.
li: beware of throughput regression if we force kernel_A for large mb. need experiment.
maya: I ran a quick canary patch forcing kernel_A for streaming only at mb<=12. results:
```
mb=8 streaming (force A) -> p95 92ms p99 115ms (good)
mb=16 streaming (force A) -> p95 210ms p99 260ms (bad)
```
aj: confirms tradeoff. so we should do adaptive policy: runtime chooses kernel by (session_type, mb, kv-warm).
nidhi: can we detect kv-warm cheaply? maybe track per-client hit-rate or recent kv-misses and use that as a feature.
simon: add a cheap heuristic: if recent_kv_miss_rate > 0.05 -> delay kernel_B for next N requests.
li: also, change prefetch to lookahead 1 message for streaming handshakes (non-blocking D2H/H2D overlap). push memcpy earlier.
maya: I prototyped handshake prefetch (lookahead=1): reduced memcpy blocking by ~35% in the trace and dropped p99 for mb=8 to ~140ms without kernel hints.
aj: nice. can you attach the experimental flags and perf artifacts? we'll put a canary on staging.
maya: flags used:
```
--streaming-handshake-prefetch=1
--kernel-select-hysteresis=enable
--kernel-pref=prefer_A_for_streaming_mid_mb
```
perf-bot: canary run queued: build/ci/3349990000-canary
nidhi: next steps:
- staging canary with both prefetch and hysteresis (maya)
- metric dashboards: p95/p99 by session_type x mb (aj)
- add KV-miss feature to routing heuristics (li)
- investigate kernel_B temp buffer path for possible optimization (simon)

maya: I'll push the canary later today and post results. thanks team :thumbsup:
aj: thanks — if canary looks good we should add an automatic rollback window and monitor p99 at 1h/24h.
simon: also log kernel choice per-inference for 24h to catch other knees. don't keep forever.
maya: agreed. I'll include short TTL in the log: kernel_choice_event with 3h retention in staging.
perf-bot: reminder: add reproducible script in repo: tools/perf/repro/3349990000.sh
maya: will do. closing for now, will update when canary finishes."
